text.p: Anglo-Australian mining group RTZ-CRA said on Tuesday its mined production of both copper and gold rose by 12 percent in the first quarter of 1997 compared with a year ago.
Copper production rose to 190,300 tonnes from 170,300 tonnes in 1996's first quarter due to higher grades at Bingham Canyon in the United States and expansion at Escondida in Chile, RTZ-CRA said.
But production fell six percent when compared with 1996's fourth quarter figure of 201,700 tonnes, the group said in its first quarter production report.
Refined copper production grew by 42 percent year-on-year to 43,500 tonnes, while rising eight percent when compared with the last quarter of 1996.
Mined gold output rose to 504,000 ounces from 449,000 ounces in 1996's first quarter.
Refined gold production was up 64 percent at 36,000 ounces from 22,000 ounces in the first three months of 1996.

Coal production climbed 26 percent to 19.4 million tonnes, while aluminium output rose by eight percent to 99,200 tonnes with Australian-based subsidiary Comalco Ltd 10 percent ahead in production and 20 percent in sales volume.
Iron ore production increased by one percent to 13.17 million tonnes, the mining group said.
Borate production fell three percent to 148,000 in the first quarter of 1997, while diamond output dropped 39 percent to 4.2 million carats from 6.849 million a year ago.
RTZ-CRA produced 3.939 million ounces of silver in the first quarter, which was 60 percent more than in the same period last year.
Uranium production increased by 30 percent to 514,000 tonnes.
